'''Richard Mansergh Thorne''' (July 25, 1942 – July 12, 2019) was an American physicist and a distinguished professor in the department of atmospheric and oceanic sciences at UCLA. He was known for his contributions to space plasma physics. He was a fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]].

Thorne graduated from Birmingham University in 1963 with a BS in mathematical physics.<ref name="AGU-SPA">{{cite journal|last=Gilbert |first=C. |title=Richard Thorne obituary |url=https://spa.agu.org/spa-section-newsletter-volume-xxvi-issue-43/ |journal=American Geophysical Union SPA Section Newsletter |volume=XXVI |issue=43 |date=July 15, 2019}}</ref> In 1968 he received a PhD in physics from MIT. The astronomer [[Alar Toomre]] was his advisor; his thesis was titled ''On the distribution of interstellar gas in the galaxy.''<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Thorne |first=Richard |title=On the distribution of interstellar gas in the galaxy. |url=http://library.mit.edu/item/000599410 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=1968}}</ref>

In 1968 Thorne joined the department of meteorology at UCLA (now the department of atmospheric and oceanic sciences). In 2000 he was appointed distinguished professor<ref name="AGU-SPA" /> and elected a fellow of the American Geophysical Union.<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard M Thorne |url=https://honors.agu.org/honorsfellow/2643-thorne/ |publisher=American Geophysical Union |accessdate=21 July 2019}}</ref> He retired in 2015.<ref name="AGU-SPA" />
